rule: Each single colored dot is extended into a full-width horizontal line in its row; the grid's outer frame is drawn and each frame cell takes the color of the dot whose row is nearest (1-D Voronoi over rows, ties go to the upper dot).
operator: Y[r,c] = col(argmin_d |r - r_d|, tie->upper) if r in {r_d} ∪ {0,H-1} or c in {0,W-1}, else 0

rule: Each 8-colored frame (itself mirror-symmetric, with notches marking its axes) contains a half-drawn 2-pattern; the pattern is completed by reflecting it across the frame's center lines so the content becomes symmetric under the frame's own reflections.
operator: for each 8-component o with bbox B_o: Y|B_o = X|B_o ∨ (2-cells of X|B_o closed under the D2 group {id, flipLR, flipTB, rot180} about the bbox center)

rule: The grid is a doubly periodic wallpaper with some rectangular patches blanked to 0; the output restores the blanked cells from the period.
operator: find smallest (p_y,p_x) with X[r,c]=X[r',c'] whenever both nonzero and (r,c)≡(r',c') mod p; Y[r,c] = tile[r mod p_y, c mod p_x]

rule: A gray (5) panel holds single colored dots arranged like a minimap of the free-standing shapes; each shape is recolored with the color of the dot occupying the corresponding relative position in the panel.
operator: segment panel P (largest object) and shapes S_j; match key dots k_i ∈ P to shapes by relative position (normalized coordinates / row-major order); Y = X with S_{σ(i)} recolored to color(k_i)

rule: Every blue (1) shape has exactly one non-blue shape of identical form (up to translation); each blue shape is recolored with its twin's color.
operator: objects O; for blue b: Y|b = color(o*) where o* = the unique non-blue o with shape(o) = shape(b) (translation-normalized cell set)

rule: Two black windows sit in an 8-background: one holds a pattern containing one uniquely colored anchor cell, the other is empty except for a single cell of that anchor color. Output is the sparse window cropped out, with the pattern translated so its anchor lands on the lone marker.
operator: windows W_1,W_2 = components of (X≠8); T = argmin_W |nonzero(W)|, S = other; m = marker in T, a = cell of color(m) in S; Y = crop(T) ∨ shift_{m−a}(S)

rule: A framed wallpaper (two rows/cols of 1, one of 4, then a cyclic color sequence constant along anti-diagonals, with a fixed 3-2-1 seed in the corner) has rectangular holes of 0; the holes are restored by the pattern's period, including holes that cut into the frame.
operator: Y[p] = X[p + k·(P,0)] (rows ≥3) or X[p + k·(0,P)] (cols ≥3) for any known orbit member, P = cycle length of the anti-diagonal sequence (7,4,9,5)

rule: Each yellow (4) rectangle contains n cells of some color c; a solid border of color c and thickness n is drawn around the rectangle.
operator: for each object o: n = #{p∈o: X[p]≠4}, c = that color; Y = X ∨ c·1[0 < d_∞(p, bbox(o)) ≤ n]

rule: Any two blue (1) cells on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal blue segment; every magenta (6) cell lying on such a segment emits a full-length magenta line along the perpendicular diagonal. 6s off the segments and unpaired 1s are left alone.
operator: for 1-pairs (a,b) with |Δr|=|Δc|: Y ∨= 1·seg(a,b); for 6-cells s ∈ seg(a,b): Y ∨= 6·line(s, d⊥), d⊥ = (Δr,−Δc)/|Δr| extended to the border

rule: A blue (1) column splits the grid into two 6x4 halves; the output is their cellwise OR, drawn in 8.
Each object (8-connected component) is translated to the right by its own bounding-box width.
operator: Y = Σ_o shift_{(0, w(o))} X_o, w(o) = bbox width of o

rule: The 3x3 objects are cropped and concatenated into a strip, ordered by position along the axis in which they are spread out (left-to-right if spread horizontally, top-to-bottom if spread vertically).
operator: objects o_i with bboxes; axis a = argmax spread of bbox origins; Y = concat_a(crop(o_σ(1)), …, crop(o_σ(n))), σ sorts by coordinate along a

rule: Figure-ground inversion: foreground cells become 0 and background cells take a color fixed by the foreground color (8→2, 3→1, 5→4).
operator: c = the unique nonzero color of X; Y[p] = g(c)·1[X[p]=0], g = {8:2, 3:1, 5:4}

rule: A 3x3 template of 4s and 6s appears once in a noisy grid. Every other 3x3 window (clipping at the grid edge allowed) whose 6-cells match the template's 6-cells exactly under some rotation/reflection has the template's 4-cells painted in, overwriting the noise.
operator: T = 3x3 window of {4,6} cells; for g ∈ D4, window w: if 1[X|w=6] = 1[gT=6] then Y|w ← 4 on {gT=4} (cross-correlation template match in clutter)

rule: A corner box fenced by gray (5) lines holds a legend of differently colored shapes; every green (3) shape outside is recolored with the color of the legend shape it equals up to rotation/reflection.
operator: legend L = objects in the 5-fenced corner; for each 3-object o: Y|o = color(ℓ), ℓ ∈ L with canon_D4(shape ℓ) = canon_D4(shape o)

rule: Blue (1) grid lines divide the canvas into a lattice of empty cells; cells in the outermost ring of the lattice are filled with 2 and all inner cells with 3.
operator: regions R_ij = 0-components indexed by lattice position (i,j) ∈ [0,m)×[0,n); Y|R_ij = 2 if i∈{0,m−1} ∨ j∈{0,n−1} else 3

rule: The single multicolored object is rotated 180 degrees about its gray (5) cell, which stays fixed.
operator: p5 = position of color 5; Y[2·p5 − p] = X[p] for all nonzero p (point reflection centered at a content-defined anchor)

rule: A red (2) rectangle is surrounded by scattered marker dots. Every row and column of the rectangle is extended outward to the grid edge on each side, except where a marker lies in that stripe on that side; such a stripe is left out entirely rather than stopped at the marker.
operator: R = bbox(2); for each boundary row/col ℓ of R and direction d: if ray(ℓ,d) ∩ markers = ∅ then Y ∨= 2·ray(ℓ,d) to border (all-or-nothing ray cast)

rule: Inside a hollow gray (5) square, concentric square rings are drawn by depth from the frame with the color cycle 5,2,5,0 (frame, red ring, gray ring, empty gap, repeat).
operator: d(p) = Chebyshev distance from p to the frame boundary (inside bbox); Y[p] = [5,2,5,0][d(p) mod 4]
missing: The depth-mod-4 rule matches 4 of 5 pairs including the test, but in train 0 (9x9 frame) the single center cell at depth 4 is 0 instead of 5, while the center cell at depth 8 in the 17x17 example is 5. I found no rule that also accounts for this cell (it may be an inconsistency in the data).

rule: In a noisy grid, pairs of 2x2 azure (8) blocks sit on the same two rows; the 2-row strip strictly between each pair is cut out, and the strips are stacked top to bottom.
operator: B = {2x2 all-8 windows}; pair b,b' ∈ B with equal rows; Y = vstack_{pairs by row} X[r:r+2, c_b+2 : c_b']

rule: Red (2) lines carry some 3x3 green nodes (green ring around a red center). Through each node a blue (1) line is drawn perpendicular to its red line, across the whole grid; wherever the blue line crosses another red line, a blue 3x3 ring is stamped around the crossing (its center stays red).
operator: nodes n = matches of the 3x3 node pattern; ℓ_n = full line through center(n) ⊥ orientation of the 2-line at n; Y = X ∨ 1·(ℓ_n \ n) ∨ 1·ring_3x3(q) for q ∈ ℓ_n ∩ {X=2}

rule: An azure (8) legend strip holds small 3x3 glyphs, one per color. Each 5x5 box carrying a blue 3x3 glyph pattern is filled solid with the color of the legend glyph it matches up to rotation/reflection. Conversely, each box that is already solid in a legend color is redrawn as that color's glyph (blue on red, in the legend's orientation).
operator: legend map g: color ↦ 3x3 glyph; for patterned box b: Y|b = c with canon_D4(g(c)) = canon_D4(inner(b)); for solid box of color c: Y|b = 2-box with inner 1·g(c) (bidirectional key lookup)

rule: A top legend pairs each color dot with the 2x2 blue shape diagonally below-right of it. Below is a lattice of 2x2 gray tiles, some with a colored corner cell. The output keeps the tile lattice (tiles separated by one blank line): each tile with color c becomes c's legend shape drawn in c, and plain gray tiles become blank.
operator: legend S: c ↦ 2x2 mask; tiles T_ij (2x2 gray blocks, lattice index (i,j)); Y[3i:3i+2, 3j:3j+2] = c·S(c) if T_ij contains color c else 0

rule: The grid is a doubly periodic stripe pattern (blue rows alternating with rows of a repeating color sequence) with rectangular holes of 0; the holes are filled from the period.
operator: smallest period (2,p) consistent with all nonzero cells; Y[r,c] = tile[r mod 2, c mod p]

rule: A complete two-color 4x4 quadrant sits at the top-left of an 8x8 block. The other three quadrants are its left-right mirror, top-bottom mirror and 180-degree rotation, each recolored by a color map read off the few hint cells already present in that quadrant (colors with no hint become 0).
operator: Q_TR = φ_TR∘flipLR(Q_TL), Q_BL = φ_BL∘flipTB(Q_TL), Q_BR = φ_BR∘rot180(Q_TL); φ_q inferred from hint cells (g(Q_TL)[p] ↦ X_q[p]), unmapped → 0

rule: Each green h x w rectangle spawns two diagonal staircases of copies running downward to the left and to the right, each copy offset from the previous one by (h, ±w), continuing until it leaves the grid (clipped at the edges).
operator: Y = ∨_o ∨_{t≥0, s=±1} shift_{t·(h_o, s·w_o)} X_o (clipped to the grid)

rule: A gray bar of length n sits in column 0 and k full-height colored stripes stand at the right. The stripes are replaced by a single column, placed just left of the first stripe, that cycles through the stripe colors in runs of n rows; the gray bar stays.
operator: n = #{X=5}, (s_1..s_k) = stripe colors left→right, c* = first stripe col − 1; Y[r,c*] = s_{⌊r/n⌋ mod k + 1}, Y[X=5] = 5, else 0

rule: A 3x3 blue/azure block has a yellow (4) dot touching one of its corners diagonally, plus an L-shaped trio of yellow dots further off that points toward another corner. The block is rotated by the quarter-turns that carry the touching dot's corner onto the L's corner; only one yellow dot remains, at the new corner.
operator: corner a = corner of bbox(B) diagonal to a 4; corner b = quadrant of the L-trio's elbow; q = cw quarter-turns from a to b; Y = rot90^{-q}(B) in place, 4 at corner b, other 4s erased

rule: An azure (8) pattern is anchored at a green (3) cell, and red (2) cells mark target anchor positions. The output holds only copies of the 8-pattern translated so that the anchor lands on each red cell; the original pattern, anchor and markers are erased.
operator: a = pos(3), S = {X=8}; Y = 8·∨_{m ∈ {X=2}} shift_{m−a}(S)  (convolution of the 2-marker set with the pattern centered at the anchor)

rule: An azure (8) wall line (possibly with gaps) splits scattered dots into two sides. Each dot falls toward the wall; dots in the same column/row merge into a single dot next to the wall, and dots whose line meets a gap in the wall disappear.
operator: for each line ℓ ⊥ wall with wall cell w_ℓ = 8, per side s: Y[w_ℓ + s] = dot if ∃ dot in ℓ on side s; all other dots erased (OR-projection/gravity onto the obstacle)

rule: The 30x30 grid is a 32x32 pattern (offset 2) with mirror symmetries r->31-r and c->31-c, partly occluded by a solid rectangle of 8s; output is the hidden content of that rectangle. In the test 8 cells have no in-grid mirror image and must come from a secondary diagonal (transpose) symmetry that holds only between certain 8x8 blocks.
operator: M = bbox{X==8}; Y = (X filled on M from orbit under G=<r->31-r, c->31-c> (+ block-local transpose where orbit is empty))|_M

rule: The grid is divided by frame lines into strip panels, each holding a 1D-periodic pattern (along the strip's long axis) with a few corrupted cells; the output repairs each strip so it is exactly periodic.
operator: For each framed panel P: find smallest period p along long axis s.t. per-phase majority is consistent; Y|_P[i] = mode{X|_P[j] : j ≡ i mod p}

rule: Left of the 4-divider is a 2-column list of 3x3 glyphs, each color standing for a stroke (1: 3 cells right, 2: 2 cells left, 3: 4 cells left, 6: 2 cells down). Starting under the 5 in the right panel, the glyphs are read column-major and drawn as a connected turtle path, each stroke starting one row below the previous stroke's end; output is the right panel.
operator: glyph sequence g_1..g_n = column-major order of 3x3 objects left of divider; state s_0 = pos(5); s_k = s_{k-1} + down + stroke(color(g_k)); Y = right panel with union of strokes painted

rule: Separator lines cut the grid into regions; each region has a short diagonal run of seed colors starting at one of its corners (the corner cell may be background). The region is repainted as concentric bands by Chebyshev distance to the region boundary, cycling through the seed colors read from the corner inward.
operator: R = components of X != wall; d(p) = Chebyshev dist from p to complement of its region (incl. outside grid); Y[p] = s_R[(d(p)-1) mod L_R], s_R = colors on corner diagonal of R

rule: Every L-tromino shoots a diagonal ray from its corner cell, pointing away from its missing cell. The ray travels diagonally and bounces like a billiard ball off any object it touches orthogonally in its direction of travel (that velocity component flips), and from the bounce cell on it takes the color of the object it bounced off; it stops at the grid edge.
operator: for each L-tromino o: x_0 = corner(o), v = corner - missing; x_{t+1} = x_t + v; if X[x+(v_r,0)]≠0: v_r←-v_r, col←X[x+(v_r,0)]; same for column; paint col along path until exit

rule: A thick band with ragged notches is surrounded by loose pieces. Pieces are translated (never rotated) to stack into chains that plug into a band notch: each piece's leading profile exactly complements the notch or the previous piece, so band plus chain has no gaps. Notches that no piece fits stay empty.
operator: find translations t_o such that band ∪ ⋃_o (o + t_o) is disjoint and gap-free along each chain (profile(o_k) = complement(profile(o_{k-1}))); Y = band ∪ ⋃ (o + t_o)

rule: In each line (rows or columns, whichever axis carries the seeds), the first two same-colored cells from the edge define a start and a period. The arithmetic progression is continued away from that edge; if a different-colored cell lies on the progression, the progression stops there and takes that cell's color. An off-lattice odd cell is left alone and the progression runs to the far edge.
operator: per line ℓ: a=pos of edge cell, p = gap to next same color; L = {a + kp}; if ∃ cell q∈L with other color c': Y on L∩[a,q] = c' else Y on L = c

rule: Every placement of a 5-cell plus (center and its 4 orthogonal neighbours) made entirely of color 4 is recolored to 8; all other cells are unchanged.
operator: Y[p] = 8 if ∃q ∈ p+{0,±e1,±e2} with X[q+δ]=4 ∀δ∈{0,±e1,±e2}; else X[p]  (morphological opening of [X=4] by the plus)

rule: A top-left legend of 2x2 blocks gives a cyclic color sequence. From each start cell on the left edge, a staircase path runs through the main region: right until the next cell is background, then up until blocked, then right again, and so on. Path cells are painted with the sequence cyclically, every blocking background cell is marked with the color of the separate 2x2 marker block, and the path stops at the grid edge or when the first step after a turn is blocked. The legend and marker block are erased.
operator: s = legend colors; walk x_0 = start, dir ∈ {→,↑} alternating on block; Y[x_k] = s[k mod |s|]; Y[blocked cell] = marker color; erase legend & marker

rule: A straight wall line splits the grid; in each row, the colored runs on one side of the wall are projected to the empty side as dotted patterns: a run of length L puts its color on every L-th cell starting right next to the wall. Where patterns collide, the run nearer the wall wins.
operator: per row, for run (c, L) on near side: Y[w + kL + 1] = c for k ≥ 0 (w = wall col, mirrored for left side), painted far-to-near so nearest run has priority

rule: There are two 4-colored pieces on a 1 background, each with 7 marker cells. The second piece is translated so that its cells adjacent to its own 7s land exactly on the first piece's 7 cells (glue joint); 7s are removed, and the output is the bounding box of the joined shape on background 1.
operator: t = pos(7_A) − (pos(7_B) + n_B), n_B = unit step from B's 7 into B; Y = crop_bbox( A\7 ∪ (B\7 + t) ) on background 1

rule: The input shows the first terms of a sequence of figures that grow by a fixed step (one more unit, column or level each time) while their colors cycle. Two 5-colored corner brackets mark a viewport placed where a later term of the sequence would sit (in train 2, two terms ahead). The output is the content of that viewport after extrapolating the sequence.
operator: terms T_k = (shape_k, color_k) with shape_k = grow^k(shape_0), color_k = c[k mod m]; render T_k at its extrapolated position; Y = crop to box spanned by the two 5-brackets

rule: The grid is a mosaic of solid color regions containing T-shaped arrows made of 1s. Each arrow sits in a source region and points into a neighbouring target region, which is recolored to the arrow's center color if that center is not 1, otherwise to the source region's original color; arrows and noise are absorbed into their region's new color. If a 3-cell corner glyph of 9s is present, the whole grid is also rotated 90° (CW for the glyph '999/9../9..', CCW for '999/..9/..9').
operator: regions R_i; arrows a: (src(a), tgt(a), center(a)); color'(tgt) = center(a) if ≠1 else color(src); Y = rot_{±90 or 0}(paint regions with color'), rotation chosen by the 9-corner glyph

rule: A 4-colored marker bar on one edge defines a band perpendicular to it and a phase origin. At distance d from the marker along the band: odd d erases objects inside the band; even d paints the band 4, except d ≡ 4 (mod 6), where the band and every object cell in that whole line become 3. Test 1 has the marker on a side edge, so the rule is applied transposed.
operator: d(p) = |line(p) − line(marker)|; Y[p] = bg if p∈band & d odd; 4 if p∈band & d even & d≢4 (6); 3 if d≡4 (6) & (p∈band or X[p]=obj); else X[p]

rule: Small single-color shapes sit to the left of a frame whose top row and side column carry colored marker cells acting as coordinates. Each shape whose color appears on both borders is moved, centered, to every (marker row, marker column) intersection of its color, being copied when there are several; shapes without markers stay put. Where placed shapes overlap, the shape listed higher on the left wins.
operator: for shape o of color c: rows R_c = {r: X[r, right]=c}, cols C_c = {k: X[top,k]=c}; if both nonempty: erase o, paint o centered at each (r,k) ∈ R_c×C_c (painted bottom-up so upper shapes win)

rule: Every output is the same 20x20 two-color master picture, under some D4 transform and color swap. Each input is a literal crop of its output, so the task is to find the unique transform, color bijection and offset at which the input fragment occurs in the master, then output the whole master in that frame. The master itself is known only from the training outputs, not from the input.
operator: M = fixed 20x20 prototype (shared by all train outputs); find (g∈D4, σ∈Sym(colors), t) unique with X = crop_t(σ∘g·M); Y = σ∘g·M  (inverse crop / template retrieval)

rule: Each black-bordered box of 5s and 7s has a 9 bar attached on one side, and a second 9 bar further along that direction. The box and its attached bar slide toward the far bar by n = min(number of 5s in the box, distance until the bars merge). n of the 5s turn into 7s, filling from the leading edge in a fill order that rotates with the direction of motion; a box with no 5s does not move.
operator: per box b: n = min(#5(b), gap(attached bar, far bar)); Y = shift_{n·dir}(b ∪ attached bar); convert first n 5s → 7 in order ρ_dir(row-major from leading edge)

rule: The 1s behave as a conserved volume of liquid. They are removed from where they sit (on a ramp, or stacked above a wall's top) and poured under gravity: running down the ramp, dropping into the first basin between walls, filling it from the bottom, then spilling over the lower rim into the next basin until the volume is used up.
operator: liquid simulation to a fixed point: volume V = #1(X); flow from source along walls with gravity; fill basins bottom-up in order of arrival, overflow via lowest rim; Y = walls ∪ settled liquid (|liquid| = V)

rule: A line of 1s and a line of 2s on two adjacent edges fix the reading frame: rotate the grid so the 2-line is on the left, giving 2-thick bands of blocks. Blocks are read band by band starting nearest the 1-line, each band read away from the 2-side, and stacked vertically in that order, each centered in a column as wide as the widest block (padding 8).
operator: g ∈ D4 with g(2-line) = left edge; objects o_1..o_n of g·X sorted by (band distance from 1-line, position from 2-side); Y = vstack_k center_W(o_k), W = max width

rule: Each horizontal 777 between the 8-rows becomes a plus: 8,6,8 in its row plus 6s directly above and below the center in the adjacent 8-rows. The 3 end-markers of the 8-rows act as balls: each rolls inward, drops through the first bar leading down into the next 8-row and reverses direction, repeating until it reaches a segment end. A ball whose first obstacle is a bar coming from above stays put. Balls collecting at the same end stack inward as 3s.
operator: Y0 = local rewrite 777→plus; for each 3: state (row, col, dir); repeat: scan dir to first 6; if bar-top: row+=2, dir=-dir; else stop; settle at segment end; Y = Y0 with stacked 3s at settle points

rule: The input holds 4x4 squares that are either hollow outlines or solid. The output is a two-column stack: hollow squares in the left column and solid squares in the right column, each column ordered by the squares' vertical position (top row) in the input, with empty 4x4 cells padding the shorter column.
operator: H = sort_by_top{o: hollow}, S = sort_by_top{o: solid}; Y = [[H_k, S_k]]_{k=1..max(|H|,|S|)} as 4x4 tiles (missing → 0)

rule: A central hub is a 4x4 ring whose four sides are 2-cell pairs of different colors. Every loose shape whose color matches a hub side is rotated so that its narrow 2-wide end faces the hub, then moved to dock, centered, against that side. Shapes with no matching side are deleted.
operator: hub sides s_c (color c, outward normal n_c); for shape o of color c: choose g∈rotations with g(narrow end of o) facing −n_c; Y = hub ∪ ⋃ (g·o placed adjacent to s_c, centered)

rule: Hand-drawn wobbly closed curves and blobs of one color are redrawn as a clean schematic with the same topology: every closed curve becomes a rectangular ring, every blob becomes a single dot, containment is preserved, and siblings keep their relative left/right/above/below arrangement, all with uniform 1-cell gaps on the background color.
operator: T = containment tree of curves/blobs with relative positions; Y = render(T): leaf→1x1 dot, curve→ring around children laid out on a grid with 1-cell gaps (snapped to aligned rows/cols)
missing: Exact layout rule for siblings (grid snapping and alignment across levels, outer padding) inferred by eye, not formalized; also re-rendering an abstract structure is not a taxonomy class

rule: Vertical bars of different colors cross a horizontal 6-line. Their vertical extents (lengths) are permuted so they increase from left to right: each bar keeps its column, width and color but takes the sorted length (and vertical span).
operator: bars b_1..b_n left→right with extents e_i; π = argsort(|e|); Y: bar i drawn with color(b_i), columns(b_i), vertical span e_{π(i)}

rule: In a maze of 1-corridors on 3-walls, a k×k black block and a k×k 2-block sit at two ends of the path. The black block slides along the corridor route toward the 2-block as far as a k×k block physically fits, stopping just before the first narrowing; if nothing blocks it, it lands on and replaces the 2-block. The black block's starting cells become corridor (1).
operator: F = erosion of corridor by k×k; path P from start to target in corridor; t* = last point of P with block ∈ F (reachable in F); Y = X with 0-block moved to t*, old cells → 1 (2-block replaced if t* = target)

rule: Same-colored dots are vertices of a polygon: taken in angular order around their centroid, consecutive dots are joined by straight lines when the join is horizontal, vertical or 45° (other joins are skipped, so a color may give an open path or nothing). A lone dot of another color touching a vertex gives a copy of that polygon translated by the touching offset in the lone dot's color, drawn beneath the original.
operator: for color c: P_c sorted by angle about centroid; S_c = ⋃ seg(p_j,p_{j+1}) over octilinear consecutive pairs; companion q (color k) with |q−v|∞=1 for v∈P_c: paint S_c + (q−v) in k, then S_c in c

rule: 6 behaves like falling liquid from the sources at the top: a 6 cell above empty space falls down, and a 6 cell resting on a horizontal 2-bar spreads left and right along the bar's top, wrapping one cell past each end and then falling again. This repeats to a fixed point.
operator: iterate to fixed point: X[r,c]=6 ∧ X[r+1,c]=7 ⇒ X[r+1,c]←6; X[r,c]=6 ∧ X[r+1,c]=2 ⇒ X[r,c±1]←6 (if 7)

rule: The grid is a lattice of framed panels. In each row of panels all panels are identical except one, and the output stacks the odd-one-out panel of each row into a single column (keeping the frame lines).
operator: panels P_{ij} from separator lines; for each row i: j* = unique j with P_{ij} ∉ {P_{ik}: k≠j}; Y = vstack_i P_{i j*}

rule: The input has two versions of one figure: a clean single-color outline, and a distorted copy (rows missing or shifted) whose compartments are colored. The output is the clean outline cropped to its bounding box, with each of its enclosed holes filled uniformly by the color of the corresponding compartment in the distorted colored copy.
operator: A = single-color component (structure), B = multicolor component (key); holes h_j of A; Y = crop(A) with h_j ← color(B-region matched to h_j)
missing: Checked that the output is A's outline with uniformly filled holes, but the exact matching of holes to B's regions under B's distortion (unequal sizes) was only done by eye, not formalized

rule: Each open host shape (arch, chevron, cup) has stray cells of another color inside its bounding region. Those cells are removed and re-emitted as a straight line of the same number of cells, starting at the host's tip on the closed side (opposite its opening) and pointing outward, clipped at the grid edge. Stray cells outside the host are untouched.
operator: host h, intruders I_h = other-color cells within bbox(h); d_h = direction opposite to opening of h, tip t_h = extreme cell of h along d_h; Y = X − I_h + {t_h + k·d_h : k=1..|I_h|} (color of I_h, clipped)

rule: Framed boxes each hold a colored inner square; a legend row lists a sequence of colors. For each consecutive legend pair (c_i, c_{i+1}) draw a bridge in color c_i, as wide as the inner square, across the gap between the box with c_i and the aligned neighbouring box with c_{i+1}.
operator: Y = X + Σ_i paint_{c_i}(span(inner(b_i), inner(b_{i+1})) ∩ gap), b_i = box whose inner color = legend[i], chain walked along the legend; bridges are axis-aligned between adjacent aligned boxes

rule: Each 3-cell chevron (V or L) points in one of 8 directions (away from its arms). Mark the cell 5 steps from its apex in that direction: 9 if one arrow hits it, 1 if two arrows converge there; if the mark lands on another chevron, that whole chevron turns 9.
operator: for object o: d(o) = -sign(Σ arm offsets from apex), t(o) = apex(o) + 5·d(o); Y[t] = 9 if |{o: t(o)=t}|=1, 1 if ≥2; if t ∈ object o', Y[o'] = 9

rule: The input holds scattered fragments of one bordered picture (outer frame of one color with inner rectangular frames) plus a small 3-cell marker touching one fragment's corner. The fragments are translated and fitted together like a jigsaw into a single rectangle whose corner stays at the marked fragment; the marker and the original fragment positions are erased.
operator: Y = bg + Σ_o shift_{t_o} X_o with {t_o} solving a tiling/fit problem: pieces disjoint, union = rectangle R with frame-color boundary and closed inner frames, t_anchor = 0 for the piece touching the marker
missing: Exact fitting criterion (edge matching / closing of inner frames) and uniqueness of the assembly; amounts to a constraint search not captured by the listed classes

rule: The input is a stack of uniform horizontal stripes (N rows). The output is a 2(N-1) square of concentric square rings: the ring at Chebyshev distance d from the border takes the color of input row d (the last row is dropped; row N-2 is the 2x2 center).

Border markers (2) define cut lines through a 7-shape. Each line is drawn from its marker to the far end of the shape along that row/column (2, with shape cells on it kept 7). The pieces on either side of the cut(s) are each pushed flush into the grid corner of their region on the marker side; in the two-marker example the quadrant touching no marker edge vanishes.
operator: L = ray(marker) up to last shape cell; pieces P_s = S∖L split by side s of the lines; Y = line(L) + Σ_s shift_{corner(s) - bbox_corner(P_s)} P_s (drop P_s whose corner lies on no marker edge)

rule: A comb of 5s on the left (base row plus teeth of varying heights) is erased and re-inserted into the box on the right, its teeth aligned under the box's content columns. Each column's stack of colored cells is pushed up so it rests on top of its tooth; whatever is pushed past the box's top row is lost.
operator: comb' = shift_(0,+10)(comb); for each content column j: stack s_j (top-aligned, length L) is placed at rows [top(tooth_j)-L, top(tooth_j)-1] clipped to rows ≥ 1; Y = box ∪ comb' ∪ pushed stacks

rule: Rectangles are outlined in 0; colored marker cells sit diagonally inside some corners. One corner in each grid already carries a finished decoration (a small pattern around the corner, in the marker's color). The same decoration, reflected to each corner's orientation and recolored to that corner's marker color, is added at every other marked corner.
operator: T = pattern at the exemplar corner, in that corner's frame; for each corner k with marker m_k: Y |= paint_{color(m_k)}(c_k + R_k·T), R_k ∈ D4 the reflection taking the exemplar corner orientation to k's

rule: On a periodic noise background, two large colored frames each hold two framed squares. In one frame the two squares form a before/after example; in the other frame one square has content and one is empty. The output (interior-sized) is the content square under the demonstrated transformation, which differs per pair: connect the dots with lines, complement, 4-fold mirror completion with fill, or copy with color substitution.
operator: Segment frames → squares (S1,S2 example, Q query, E empty); induce T with T(S_before)=S_after (T ∈ {line-connect, complement, D2-symmetrize+fill, recolor-copy}); Y = T(interior(Q)) recolored to Q's palette
missing: The inner transformation T is a different operation in each pair and must be induced from a single in-grid example (meta-level program induction); which square of the example pair is 'before' is not fixed by layout

rule: Scattered fragments share identical end blocks (one or more columns/rows) with other fragments. Overlay the fragments so that matching end blocks coincide, chaining them into one connected picture (a strip in train, a 2D chain in test). The output is the bounding box of the merged picture on the background color.
operator: find translations t_o with shift_{t_o}(X_o) agreeing on all overlaps, where consecutive pieces overlap on equal boundary sub-blocks; Y = crop_bbox(⋃_o shift_{t_o} X_o) over bg

rule: Blobs of 1 carry a small two-color seed attached on one side; one blob already shows its seed repeated as a ray to the border. Each other seed is tiled periodically (period = seed length) away from its blob until the grid edge, overwriting anything in its path.
operator: for seed s (h×w block adjacent to blob b, direction d = away from b): Y[p] = s[(p - p_s) mod period along d] for all p on the ray from s to the border along d

rule: Train inputs are split into equal panels by separator columns; each panel holds isolated noise pixels plus one small shape in some orientation. The output is a single panel-sized grid showing only one copy of that shape, in a new orientation and position (in each train pair it covers one cell common to all panels). The test has no separators: one rotated copy of a hexomino amid noise, and the expected output turns it 90° CCW about its bottom-left cell.
operator: Y = bg + place(R·S, t) with S the recurring shape; the rule choosing the rotation R and the target location t is not identified
missing: How the output pose (orientation and location) of the shape is determined; the panel shapes appear in different orientations and none matches the output pose; the test lacks the panel structure entirely

rule: Single-cell anchors on the grid border define a row or column per color. Every object carrying a marker cell of an anchor color (the object's minority color, or a lone pixel) is translated perpendicular to that border until its marker lies on the anchor's row/column; cells pushed off-grid are clipped.
operator: for object o with marker m_o of color a: Y |= shift_{(line(a) - coord(m_o))·n_a} X_o, n_a = normal of the anchor's border
missing: Exact for 4 of 5 pairs; in train 1 one object is also shifted one column sideways, which the alignment rule does not explain (possibly task noise)

rule: A black panel lists key colors down its column 1 (odd rows). Output is that panel with each key row holding one dot per object of that color in the rest of the grid, at columns 1,3,5,...; objects in non-key colors are ignored.
operator: Y = crop(panel); for key k at row r_k: n_k = #components of color k outside the panel; Y[r_k, 2i+1] = k for i < n_k

rule: Solid 5x5 colored blocks sit in one area, small 3x3 patterns of various colors elsewhere. Output is the block area (with its 1-cell margin); each block gets the same-colored 3x3 pattern punched into its interior as holes (pattern cells become background). Patterns with no matching block are dropped.
operator: Y = crop(block region); for block B_c of color c with pattern P_c: Y[interior(B_c)] = c·(1 - P_c) + bg·P_c

rule: A 2-colored emitter with a 4 tip shoots a ray in its pointing direction. A blob of 1 hit by the ray turns entirely 2 and re-emits a ray (as wide as its 3-colored nozzle) out of the nozzle side; this chains until rays leave the grid. Blobs never hit are erased; everything drawn is 2.
operator: iterate: ray r_k from source along d_k until it meets blob o; Y[o] = 2; next source = nozzle(o), d = nozzle direction(o), width = |nozzle|; Y = bg + 2·(⋃ rays ∪ hit blobs)

rule: The grid has a template region (a solid color with holes cut in another color) and a palette region of colored pieces. The output is the template region with every hole filled by the piece of exactly the same shape (single-cell holes take the single 0 cells); the palette is discarded.
operator: Y = crop(template); for each hole component h: find piece p with shape(p) = shape(h) (translation-equivalent); Y[h] = shift_{bbox(h)-bbox(p)}(p)

rule: Each object slides vertically, keeping its columns, to the top or bottom edge. Objects whose shape has a twin in the grid (same shape up to rotation/reflection, hence also the same cell count) go flush to the top; objects with a unique shape go flush to the bottom.
operator: Y = Σ_o shift_{(dr_o,0)} X_o, dr_o = -top(o) if ∃o'≠o: shape(o') ≅_{D4} shape(o), else (H-1) - bottom(o)

rule: Several congruent two-cell-thick bars (rotated copies with a distinctive end pattern) lie on the grid; a few single pixels sit on the grid edge. Each edge pixel lies on the line extended from one bar's side at some offset along that bar. All bars then cast lines of every marker color at those same offsets, in their own frame, from that same side out to the grid edge.
operator: frame g_b ∈ D4 ⋉ Z^2 per bar b (from its end pattern); marker m on the ray from bar b_m gives (color c_m, offset k_m) = g_{b_m}^{-1}(m); Y = X + Σ_b Σ_m ray_{g_b(k_m)}(c_m) to the border

rule: Divider lines split the input into a top band of k×k patterns (one color each), a middle band whose union forms a small color map, and a bottom row giving one key color per column block. Output = the map blown up: each map cell of color c becomes pattern P_c (the top pattern of color c), recolored to the key color under that pattern's column; empty cells stay empty.
operator: Y = Σ_{(i,j)} E_{ij} ⊗ key[col(P_{M[i,j]})]·P_{M[i,j]} (Kronecker-style substitution; M = overlay of middle blocks)

rule: One large template block has holes of several shapes; small colored shapes are scattered elsewhere. Output is the cropped template with each hole filled by the most frequent color among scattered shapes congruent to that hole (up to rotation/reflection).
operator: Y = crop(T); for hole h: Y[h] = argmax_c #{o : color(o)=c, shape(o) ≅_{D4} shape(h)}

rule: Black shapes left of a vertical 5-line each slide right until they touch the line. Then every row where a shape touches the line and that row passes through an enclosed hole of the shape gets the part of the row right of the line painted 2.
operator: X' = Σ_o shift_{(0, line-1-right(o))} X_o; Y[r, >line] = 2 iff X'[r, line-1] = 0 ∧ ∃c: (r,c) ∈ enclosed-hole(X')

rule: The grid has colored border strips and separators. Each 8-object carries a 9 sub-pattern and colored tabs; loose 9 markers lie elsewhere. Each object is rotated/reflected and moved so its 9 cells land exactly on a matching 9 marker, with each colored tab facing the border strip of the same color; the original copies are erased.
operator: for object o: choose g ∈ D4 with direction(tab_c) under g = side(border_c) for each tab color c, and t with t + g·nine(o) = marker m; Y = bg_panels + Σ_o (t + g)·X_o

rule: A large concentric multi-color figure is cropped out; small loose pixels elsewhere act as a key. Each color layer of the figure is rotated clockwise about the figure's center by 90° times the number of loose pixels of that color (0 if none).
operator: Y = Σ_c R_{90°}^{n_c}(crop(X)·[X=c]), n_c = #loose cells of color c outside the main object, rotation about the crop center

rule: A binary image of 1-regions and 0-regions carries pixel noise. Stray 1-specks in 0 areas are erased. Stray 0-specks in 1 areas (single holes, notches, tiny clusters) are kept, and their 8-neighbourhood is painted 7 as a ring.
operator: N1 = {1-cells with ≤1 one-neighbour}, X' = X − N1; D = {0-cells in 0-components of size ≤3 or with ≤1 zero 4-neighbour}; Y = X' with Y[dilate_3x3(D) ∖ D] = 7
missing: Exact definition of a 'speck' versus legitimate thin structure (1-wide corridors, region corners, grid-edge cells); my local criteria match all train pairs and test 1 but miss one corner cell in test 0

rule: Four 5x5 panels: panel 1 holds a dividing line (diagonal, vertical or horizontal) plus one marker cell on one side; panels 2 and 3 hold patterns; panel 4 is empty. Panel 4 becomes panel 2 on the marker's side of the line and panel 3 on the other side; on the line itself panel 2 is overlaid on panel 3 (panel 2's non-background cells win).
operator: M_A = flood region of panel1 containing the marker (line as wall), M_B = other side, L = line; Y4[p] = P2[p] if p∈M_A; P3[p] if p∈M_B; (P2[p] if P2[p]≠bg else P3[p]) if p∈L

rule: Several parallel anti-diagonal segments are drawn on the background. Every background cell lying between two such segments (in the r+c direction) and within both segments' extents along the r-c direction is filled with 2, which shades the parallelograms between neighbouring segments.
operator: u=r+c, v=r-c; Y[p]=2 iff X[p]=bg ∧ ∃ segments i,j: u_i < u(p) < u_j ∧ v(p) ∈ [v_i^min,v_i^max] ∩ [v_j^min,v_j^max]

rule: The input is several 5x5 panels separated by 6-lines (2x2, a column or a row), each holding one colored stroke that touches some panel edges. The panels are re-laid in a single row or column (6 separators kept), ordered so that each stroke's exit point on one edge meets the next panel's stroke entry point on the facing edge. The direction of the chain (vertical or horizontal) follows which edges the strokes touch.
operator: panels P_i; edge contacts e_out(P_i), e_in(P_j); find the Hamiltonian chain with e_out(P_k)=e_in(P_{k+1}), starting at the panel with no entry contact; Y = concat_{axis}(P_{σ(1)}, sep, P_{σ(2)}, ...)

rule: Solid blocks (nodes) are joined by thin lines (edges) into a graph with cycles; exactly two nodes share a distinct color. Along the shortest route between those two nodes, the line cells are recolored 5 and the intermediate nodes recolored 3; everything else is unchanged.
operator: G = (blocks, line-paths); s,t = the two blocks of the color with count 2; π = argmin_path d_G(s,t) (BFS); Y = X with Y[edges(π)] = 5, Y[interior nodes(π)] = 3

rule: Four colored polyomino pieces are scattered; one carries a 5 cell. The output is the s×s square (s² = total cell count) exactly tiled by the four pieces, each rotated/reflected as needed, with the 5 at the top-left corner.
operator: s = sqrt(Σ|o|); find g_o ∈ D4 ⋉ Z^2 with ⊔_o g_o(o) = [0,s)^2 and g(5-cell) = (0,0); Y = Σ_o g_o X_o (exact-cover polyomino tiling)

rule: A single non-branching path is made of consecutive colored segments. The output is a one-column grid listing the path's cell colors in order from its top end to its other end (each color repeated once per cell of its segment).
operator: walk the path p_1..p_n from the top endpoint (4/8-adjacency, no branches); Y = column vector [X(p_1), ..., X(p_n)]

rule: Lines are axis-aligned segments with gaps; short diagonal pieces are noise. Every diagonal piece is erased, and wherever a 2-cell diagonal stub hangs off the end of a segment (leaning toward a gap), the 3-cell gap between that end and the next collinear segment is filled with the line color. Gaps without such a stub stay open.
operator: Y = X - Σ_{d diagonal comps} d + Σ_{s stub attached at end e of segment L} fill(gap between e and next collinear segment of L)

rule: The top area holds small multicolored objects; the bottom holds horizontal bands, each with a fill color and an end/border color. Each same-color part of each object is erased from the top and stamped into the band whose fill equals that color, at the same columns, dropped to the band's bottom row, and recolored to that band's border color.
operator: Y = erase_top(X) + Σ_{components q of color c} border(c)·shift_{(rowbot(band(c)) - rowbot(q), 0)} q, band(c) = band with fill c

rule: Each object has a red (2) part. If the red part is a straight line, the object's other cells are mirrored across that line; if it is a single cell, they are rotated 180 degrees about it. The original is kept, so each object becomes symmetric.
operator: Y = X ∪ ⋃_o σ_o(o \ red_o), σ_o = reflection across line red_o if |red_o|>1, else point reflection p -> 2·red_o - p

rule: A one-cell-wide wire network of one color joins a central 3x3 junction to several framed two-color terminal patches. Each wire branch, together with its terminal's frame, is recolored with the majority color of the terminal it leads to. The junction's 8-cell ring keeps the wire color, and its center takes the majority color among the branches attached to it.
operator: Y[p] = maj(T(branch(p))) for wire cells p ∉ ring(J); Y[center J] = argmax_c #{branches of J colored c}; T(b) = terminal reached by following branch b

rule: On a checkerboard background, each diamond ring has short colored diagonal segments lying parallel to some of its edges. From both endpoints of each segment, a ray of the segment's color is drawn diagonally outward, perpendicular to the segment and away from the diamond, to the grid border. The result looks like the outline of a beam.
operator: Y = X + Σ_{segments s, endpoints e∈{s_0,s_end}} color(s)·ray(e, n_s), n_s = diagonal unit normal of s pointing away from the diamond center

rule: The input has a tiled arrangement of solid color blocks, each dotted with k off-color cells, plus loose framed shapes whose interiors contain some number of holes (connected regions). Each shape goes into the block whose dot count equals the shape's hole count, centered with a one-cell margin of block color, and the shape's holes are filled with the block color. The output is the block arrangement alone.
operator: Y = crop_blocks(X) with block b replaced by pad_1(recolor_{holes->color(b)} S_{σ(b)}), σ(b) = shape with #holes(S) = #dots(b)

rule: Each scene has a straight anchor line, a 'rope' curve attached next to one end of it, and a nearby target object. The rope keeps its attachment cell and its cell count but is re-laid as a taut path: straight toward the target, hugging the target's 4-adjacent contour around the far side, then continuing straight in its last direction. It is clipped at the grid border.
operator: rope' = first |rope| cells of path γ(attach, T) where γ = straight approach + 4-adjacent contour of T (diagonal steps at corners) + straight continuation; Y = X - rope + rope'
missing: Exact path construction (choice of approach step and wrap side) not formalized; length preservation holds with border clipping in all pairs, but only checked by hand

rule: Small key boxes in the corners each show an arrow, made of a 1-cell line ending in a 2-cell (orthogonal or diagonal), framed in some color c. Every yellow dot inside a region outlined in color c slides in that key's direction until the next step would hit the outline.
operator: Y = X with each dot d moved: d <- d + k·v(c(d)), k = max steps before blocked; v(c) = arrow direction of the key framed in color c, c(d) = color of the enclosing outline

rule: Several overlapping rectangular frames of different colors are each divided into compartments by internal lines, with a noise color scattered over everything. The output is a bar chart with one row per frame color: that color repeated once per compartment, padded to the maximum count with the noise color, and rows sorted by ascending count.
operator: n_c = #faces(frame_c) (gaps from noise/crossings bridged); Y = rows sorted by n_c: [c]*n_c + [noise]*(max n - n_c)

rule: One large 'board' shape has holes. The other colored objects are pieces drawn at an integer scale k, and single dots are noise. Each hole is filled with the color of the piece whose downscaled shape matches the hole up to rotation or reflection, and the filled board is upscaled by k.
operator: Y = upscale_k(B + Σ_{holes h} color(P_σ(h))·1_h), σ(h) = piece with D4-canonical(downscale_k(P)) = D4-canonical(h), k = piece scale

rule: A key cell (e.g. 7 or 4, wrapped in a wire color) sits at the end of a wire that threads through a chain of small closed loops. Every loop reached by following that wire from the key, alternating wire segments and loops and passing through wire crossings, has its interior filled with the key color. Loops that merely touch other loops, sit on a different wire, or lie beyond a gap in the wire are left empty. With two keys, each fills only its own wire's loops.
operator: Y = X + Σ_keys κ Σ_{loops L ∈ Reach(κ)} color(κ)·1_{int(L)}, Reach = closure over graph {wire segments of κ's wire color} ∪ {loops}, edges = 8-adjacency segment↔loop

rule: Each U-shaped socket has an inner tooth. A red block whose width matches the tooth and which lies in line with it, in front of the socket's opening, slides toward the socket until it touches the tooth, leaving a trail of 0 over its original cells and the path. All other red blocks are erased.
operator: for socket s with tooth t opening along direction d: block b with width(b)=width(t), aligned with t on axis d: b -> shift_{k·d} b until contact; path cells := 0; unmatched red := bg

rule: Each colored object is made left-right symmetric by deleting cells: pick the vertical axis that keeps the most cells, then remove every cell whose mirror image across it is not part of the object.
operator: Y = Σ_o color(o)·(o ∩ R_{a*}(o)), a* = argmax_a |o ∩ R_a(o)|, R_a = reflection across vertical line x=a

rule: Stacked hollow rectangles each have a color c, and small scattered objects lie to their right. All scattered objects are erased. Each rectangle receives n_c dots of its color on its middle row, placed from the right inner edge leftward every 2 cells, where n_c is the number of scattered objects of color c.
operator: n_c = #components of color c outside frames; Y = frames + Σ_c Σ_{i=1..n_c} c·δ(mid_row(F_c), right(F_c) - 2i); noise erased

rule: The 6 in a corner marks a room: the 8-region connected to it, bounded by 1-walls and the grid border. Every room cell touching (8-adjacent) the border or a wall that is not an interior island becomes 7, outlining the room. 1-objects that don't touch the room are erased; islands inside the room are kept but not outlined.
operator: R = floodfill_4(non-1 cells, from 6); F = R ∪ holes(R); Y[p]=7 for p∈R with N8(p) ⊄ F (or off-grid); 1-components with no 8-contact to R -> 8

rule: Pairs of same-colored L-shaped corner markers span rectangles, and a two-column legend maps marker color a to fill color b (0 or bg means clear). Rectangles are painted in legend order with the first entry on top: each paints its bounding box with b except its own marker cells. A solid 2x2 marker block is recolored whole.
operator: for (a->b) in reversed(legend): Y[bbox(X==a) \ (X==a)] = b (b=0 -> bg); solid block: Y[bbox]=b

rule: Vertical bars have caps of color c at both ends and a different interior color. In the top-left key, a column of color c with length k selects, among the bars capped with c, the k-th tallest, and that bar's interior is recolored to c. Other bars are unchanged.
operator: for each key column (c, k): b* = k-th largest by height among bars with cap color c; Y[interior(b*)] = c

rule: A 30x30 pattern that is symmetric under transposition and under the off-center mirrors r -> 31-r and c -> 31-c has rectangular patches blanked to 0. Each blanked cell is restored from a symmetric partner.
operator: Y[p] = X[g·p] for any g ∈ G = <transpose, r->31-r, c->31-c> with X[g·p] ≠ 0

rule: Columns of identical plus-shapes stand on a baseline, and some columns have a red (2) or green (3) bar beneath them in the bottom row. Columns over red bars are recolored to gray (5). The column over the green bar is extended upward by as many copies of its shape as there are shapes in all red-bar columns combined. The bars are erased.
operator: n = Σ_{columns over red} #shapes; Y = recolor_{5}(red columns) + stack(green column, +n copies at period 4 upward); bottom bars -> bg

rule: The left border is a column of 6s, and the rows are colored bars or hook shapes separated by gap rows. For each gap row lying between two bars of the same color, the 6 at its left end is removed (becomes 7) and 'rolls' right along the gap. It follows the turns of the channel it is in, goes straight through open space, and a 6 is placed where it stops: at the grid edge, or at the first obstacle it cannot turn around.
operator: for gap rows r with color(bar r-1) = color(bar r+1): X[r,0]:=7; trajectory p_{t+1} = p_t + d_t, d turns to the single open side when blocked inside a channel; stop at edge/obstacle; Y[p_end] = 6
missing: Exact turn-vs-stop condition when blocked (it turns inside same-colored channels but stops in open space, e.g. train 2 at (7,8)) inferred from a single discriminating case; not simulated numerically

rule: Two framed panels sit on a patterned background. One panel contains complete motifs, each built around a marker cell; the other contains only lone marker cells. The output is the second panel cropped with its frame, with the matching motif stamped around each lone marker so that the marker keeps its position within the motif.
operator: Y = crop(frame_T) + Σ_{markers m in T} shift_{m - anchor(M_{color(m)})} M_{color(m)}, motifs M_c read from the source panel

rule: Each two-colored piece is moved so that one of its color parts exactly fills the hole of a matching socket shape. Matching uses the D4 isometry, translation, rotation or reflection, that makes the part fit the hole, and the rest of the piece trails outside. When the fitting isometry is a reflection, the piece's two colors swap, like a two-sided tile turned over. The original pieces are erased.
operator: for piece P=(A,B), socket hole h: find g∈D4⋉Z² with g(A)=h (or g(B)=h); Y = Y - P + recolor_{swap if det g<0}(g(P))

rule: A side panel encodes a program: a small two-color tile T, a binary mask S, a box whose 4-dot marks a corner, and a box whose 7-domino points in a direction. The output is the scene with the panel removed and a block pattern written over it: S, rotated so that its 'up' follows the 7-arrow, is expanded by the color-swapped tile (Kronecker product) and anchored at the marked corner. In the test, two such panels act independently.
operator: Y = scene; Y[corner-anchored window] ← (rot_θ S) ⊗ swap(T) where S-cells are written and others left; θ from 7-arrow, corner from 4-dot

rule: A shape of color A is accompanied by a sparse dot map on a spacing-2 lattice, with one dot of color A and the others of color B. The dot map is scaled up to the shape's bounding-box size and aligned so that the A-dot falls on the shape. Each B-dot becomes a copy of the shape in color A, the original shape is recolored to B, and the dot map is erased.
operator: Y = bg + Σ_{dots d} col'(d)·shift_{(d - d_A)/2 ⊙ size(S)} S, col'(B)=A, col'(A)=B; dots removed

rule: Terminals on one side, solid 3x3 blocks or '+' shapes, are joined by 8-colored wires to terminal slots on the opposite side, shown as 'x' shapes. At 5-cells and 9-blocks one wire passes under another. Each wire is traced from end to end. The missing terminal at either end is drawn in the color of the other end ('+' on the top/left side, 'x' on the bottom/right side), and solid blocks become '+' shapes.
operator: for each wire w (path through 8, straight through crossings 5/9): ends (a,b); Y[slot(b)] = shape_side(b) in color(a) (and vice versa); solid blocks -> plus

rule: A front rectangular frame occludes parts of other rectangle outlines, some solid and some dashed in two alternating colors. The output is the frame's interior, showing the occluded portions of those outlines: each rectangle is completed from its visible sides, and dashed outlines continue their alternation.
operator: Y = crop_{int(F)}( Σ_{R behind F} outline(bbox_completion(R)) with dash phase by parity ), F = front frame
missing: In train 2 the hidden part of the 8/9 dashed rectangle has inverted dash phase relative to parity continuation from its visible part (the 4/5 rectangle and the test follow parity); the phase rule is unexplained

rule: Every blue (1) object gets a red (2) outline on the background cells 8-adjacent to it. Objects that enclose holes are recolored: body to 8 and holes to 6. Objects without holes stay blue.
operator: Y = X + 2·(dilate_8(o) \ o \ holes(o)) ∀o; if holes(o)≠∅: Y[o]=8, Y[holes(o)]=6

rule: Key glyphs (an inner color a, an outer color b, then an 8-colored stamp shape beyond b) define rewrite rules. Every scattered cell of color a is replaced by the stamp shape in color b, placed relative to the dot as the stamp sits relative to the cell just past b. Keys are erased, and dots of colors with no key are kept.
operator: for key (a,b,S,anchor): Y = Σ_{p: X[p]=a} b·1_{p + (S - anchor)}; keys removed; other cells kept

rule: Lines of 1 split the grid into four panels: a 4-colored shape, a panel with n separate 3-objects, and two solid color panels C and D. The output repeats the shape's bounding box n times along the layout axis, with shape cells in color C and empty cells in D, and the copies are separated by one-cell gaps of D.
operator: n = #components(panel_B == 3); Y = concat_axis([recolor_{4->C, 0->D}(bbox(S))] * n, sep = D)

rule: A cross of 1s splits the grid into quadrants. The top-left quadrant holds a template: a red 2-block with colored blocks attached around it. Every other quadrant holds only a red block of some size; the template's attachments are added around it, scaled by (red block size / template red size) and mirrored to match the quadrant (left-right on the right side, top-bottom on the bottom side). Attachments are clipped at the quadrant border.
operator: for quadrant q with red block B_q: Y += σ_q( scale_{|B_q|/|B_0|}( template - B_0 ) ) anchored on B_q; σ_q ∈ {id, flip_h, flip_v, rot180}

rule: The grid contains 5x5 framed squares whose frame is 8 or 2. Frame-8 squares slide left and frame-2 squares slide right until they hit the grid edge or a square of the same frame color (stacking); squares of opposite colors pass through each other.
operator: Y = bg + Σ_o shift_{(0, s(o))} X_o, s(o) = per-color gravity: dir = left if frame(o)=8 else right, objects processed nearest-wall-first, stop at border or previously placed same-color object

rule: A stack of arches (Π shapes made of left leg, top bar, right leg, each piece one color) plus marker color(s) in row 0. Delete every piece whose color is a marker color, then let the rest settle under gravity: legs fall until resting on something; a bar stays only if something is below it or both its ends touch supported pieces, otherwise it falls. (Train 1 output has one extra 2-cell at (4,5) that no conservation-respecting rule produces; likely a data error.)
operator: Y = settle(X minus pieces with color in M), M = colors in row 0; pieces = Π-decomposition (legs incl. corners, bar between); settle = iterate: stable = least fixed point of {on floor, or above a stable cell, or bar with both end-neighbors stable}; move all unstable pieces down 1; repeat

rule: The grid is a 7x7 lattice of identical 3x3 tiles separated by lines; a few tiles are replaced by an odd tile containing a new color. The odd tile's mask of the new color is a 3x3 shape; at the macro (tile) level, place that same shape so it covers the existing odd tiles and fill all its macro cells with the odd tile (self-similar completion).
operator: T = tiles(X) (7x7 macro grid), t* = odd tile, S = 1[t* == new color] ∈ {0,1}^{3x3}; find offset o with supp(odd) ⊆ o+S (unique); Y_tile[q] = t* for q ∈ o+S, else base tile

rule: An outline shape with one open side contains a seed color. The seed color fills the shape's interior and leaks out through the opening, filling the cone bounded by extrapolating the two walls next to the opening (continuing their slope, e.g. 1 col/row, 1 col/2 rows, 2 cols/row) out to the grid edge; any other-colored obstacle in the path casts a straight shadow in the leak direction that stays unfilled.
operator: d = direction of the opening; R = interior ∪ cone between walls extended along their own slope; Y = X + seed·1[R \ (O ∪ ⋃_{o∈O} ray_d(o))], O = obstacle cells

rule: The input holds a single-color shape (mask M) and a multicolor tile T. The output is the Kronecker product: one copy of T for every filled cell of M, background elsewhere.
operator: M, T = crops of the mono- and multi-colored components; Y[p] = T[p mod |T|] if M[⌊p/|T|⌋] ≠ bg else bg (Y = 1[M] ⊗ T)

rule: A small dotted key (colored single cells on a spacing-2 lattice) in the corner describes a layout of colored blocks. A few blocks of the layout are already drawn at large scale; draw all other key cells as blocks with the same block size and spacing, anchored so the existing blocks coincide with their matching key cells.
operator: K = key matrix (dots), s = block side, p = block period from existing blocks; find offset o (unique) with existing blocks = K-blocks at o; Y = X ∪ ⋃_{(i,j): K_ij≠bg} K_ij·1[o + p(i,j) + [0,s)^2]

rule: Several copies of one figure appear, at different scales, each in one of two variants that differ in a few parts (e.g. stem/base colors, a cap on top vs a foot on the bottom, center color). Every figure is switched to the other variant, in its own frame and at its own scale.
operator: objects o = s_o·V_{k(o)} (variant k ∈ {1,2}, scale s_o, position t_o); Y = bg + Σ_o place_{t_o}(upscale_{s_o}(V_{3-k(o)})), with V_1, V_2 read off the input's own copies

rule: A 3 on the border starts a path heading straight inward; border-attached walls of 2 contain k cells of 1, and k is the clearance the path must keep from that wall. The path runs in its main direction, and before a blocking wall it turns 90°, passes the wall's free end at clearance k, then resumes the main direction, until it exits the grid; the 1s are recolored 2.
operator: walls w with clearance k_w = #1s(w); path = greedy rectilinear ray from the start in direction d, detouring around each blocking wall at offset k_w (turn k_w+1 cells before it, go to k_w+1 beyond its free end, resume d); Y = X[1→2] + 3·path

rule: Jigsaw assembly: each colored piece carries 2-colored connector dots. Keeping the 4 piece fixed, translate every other piece so that its connector dots coincide with a matching connector set (same relative geometry) of an already-placed piece, building one connected assembly.
operator: pieces P_i with connector sets K_i; find translations t_i (t_4 = 0) such that for each joint, (K_i + t_i) ∩ (K_j + t_j) matches a whole connector group; Y = Σ_i shift_{t_i}(P_i ∪ K_i)

rule: Small 3x3 badges (ring color r, center color c) are scattered with a 5-colored path that connects exactly two of them. Keep only the two badges at the path's ends (and the path); in each, the center color c is replaced by the center color of the badge whose ring color is c. All other badges are erased.
operator: badges b = (ring r_b, center c_b); E = {b : b touches an end of the 5-path}; Y = path + Σ_{b∈E} badge(r_b, c_{β(b)}) with β(b) = the badge b' with r_{b'} = c_b; other badges → bg

rule: A 3x3 key in the top-left corner (fenced by 3s) shows a set of colors. Each black rectangular region elsewhere holds scattered colored dots; a region that contains every key color is erased (filled with the 7 background), all other regions are left unchanged.
operator: S = colors(key) \ {7}; regions R = components of non-7 cells; Y = X with R := 7 for every R with S ⊆ colors(R)

rule: The top band shows 3-4 query glyphs; the middle holds a fixed 4x4 catalogue of 3x3 glyphs. Every catalogue glyph identical (shape and color) to a query glyph gets its 5x5 cell background turned to 3 (adjacent highlighted cells merge). If the highlighted glyphs make up one full row or column of the catalogue, the top band's background and the bottom strip become 3; otherwise the bottom strip becomes 2.
operator: Q = query glyphs, G_ij = catalogue glyphs; H = {(i,j): G_ij ∈ Q}; Y = X with bg→3 in cell(i,j) ∀(i,j)∈H; if H is a full row/column: top-band bg→3 and bottom strip := 3, else bottom strip := 2

rule: The four arms of a small plus (hollow center) grow outward as snakes on an unbounded plane, all at once. At each step a snake turns right (clockwise) if it can, else goes straight, else turns left, and it never comes 8-adjacent to any drawn cell except its own last two. The result is an interleaved 4-arm square spiral with 1-cell gaps (with jogs when arms are longer than 2), cropped to the grid.
operator: Y = crop_Ω(lim_t S_t), S_{t+1} = S_t ∪ {head_a + d*_a}, d*_a = first of (right, straight, left) with N_8(cell) ∩ S_t ⊆ {head_a, prev_a}; arms a = the 4 plus arms

rule: A 9x9 motif made of 3x3 blocks with an empty center block is expanded to 15x15 about its center. The outer block at macro offset 2o gets a copy of the inner block at offset -o (point reflection). The empty center block is filled with the cells at offset 2·(i,j) from the center (a stride-2 sample of the ring around the hole), and its middle cell gets the motif's most frequent color.
operator: blocks b(o), o∈{-1,0,1}^2 around center c; Y = X + Σ_{o≠0} place(c+6o, b(-o)); Y[c+(i,j)] = X[c+2(i,j)] for (i,j)≠0, Y[c] = mode(motif colors)

rule: Every pair of 1-cells on a common diagonal is joined by a diagonal segment of 1s. Each 6 lying on such a segment emits a full line of 6 along the perpendicular diagonal, out to both grid edges; 6s off the segments stay as they are.

A 2-wide legend strip touching the grid edge lists color pairs: the cell on the edge side is the key, its neighbor across the strip is the value. Each outline shape whose color is a key gets its enclosed holes filled with the mapped value; shapes with non-key colors are left alone.
operator: m: key→value from legend pairs (key on the edge side); holes H = bg components not reaching the border; Y = X + Σ_{h∈H, col(∂h)∈dom m} m(col(∂h))·1[h]

rule: A central 3x3 block (3s around a 2) sits among 6-walls and scattered 9s. The 9s reachable from the block without crossing 6 are taken nearest-first by path (BFS) distance, at most 9 of them. They are erased from their positions and fill the block's cells in reading order, center included.
operator: δ = BFS distance from the block through non-6 cells; N = the k = min(9, #reachable 9s) 9-cells with smallest δ; Y = X with N → 7 and block cells 1..k (row-major) → 9

rule: Two large solid regions of colors a and b are sprinkled with noise: stray dots outside, foreign dots and bg holes inside. Clean the noise (strays outside become bg, foreign dots inside take the region color). Every bg hole inside a region becomes 8, and its 3x3 neighborhood is painted with the partner region's color (rings may stick out past the region).
operator: R_a, R_b = cleaned region masks; holes h = bg cells inside R_c; Y = clean(X) with Y[N_8(h)\holes] = partner(c), Y[h] = 8

rule: Each marker dot is replaced by its color's fixed 4x4 glyph drawn with the dot as top-left corner, clipped at the edges: 2 → hollow 4-square, 3 → 1-ring, 5 → two diagonal 2x2 blocks of 6, 8 → 7-X. A pre-drawn sample glyph with a marker diagonally after it at (+4,+4) is a legend; it and that marker are erased.
operator: Y = Σ_{m ∈ markers \ legend} place_{pos(m)}(G[col(m)]) clipped to Ω; G = fixed color→glyph table (also shown by the legend); legend glyph and its marker → bg

rule: 4x4 boxes (a frame around a 2x2 colored core) have gaps in their frames. Each gap emits a ray of the core color: straight out from a side gap, diagonal from a corner gap, running to the grid edge. When two rays meet they run on side by side in the direction of the sum of their direction vectors (two diagonals → straight; straight + perpendicular straight → diagonal; diagonal + straight → a 2:1 slope).
operator: rays ρ_g = (start g, dir d_g ∈ {8 directions} by gap position relative to core); propagate step by step; on contact between ρ_i and ρ_j set d_i, d_j := d_i + d_j (rasterized as alternating unit steps); Y = X + Σ core_color·ρ_g
missing: Exact contact condition and rasterization of merged rays at non-45° slopes (e.g., which step comes first) only checked by eye on a few merges.

rule: A legend region (cut off by a line of 1s) shows colored templates with different numbers of holes. Every gray (5) blob is recolored with the legend color whose template has the same number of enclosed holes; blobs whose hole count is not in the legend are erased.
operator: m: #holes(template) → color(template); Y[o] = m(#holes(o)) for each 5-component o (holes = bg components enclosed by o), or bg if #holes(o) ∉ dom m

rule: Several parallel line segments (horizontal, vertical or diagonal) have one end aligned on a common perpendicular line. Each segment is extended or trimmed at its free end to the length of the middle segment (by position), keeping the aligned end fixed.
operator: segments s_1..s_n ordered across the direction of the lines, L* = len(s_{⌈n/2⌉}); Y = bg + Σ_i col(s_i)·seg(anchor_i, dir, L*)

rule: One outline template (or two adjacent ones) has empty slots inside its bounding box, and small colored pieces are scattered elsewhere. Crop to the template's bounding box and fill every slot with the scattered piece of exactly that shape (jigsaw fit, no rotation), giving a symmetric picture.
operator: T = template bbox crop, S = bg components inside T (slots), P = pieces; find bijection σ: S→P with shape(s) = shape(σ(s)) (up to translation); Y = T + Σ_s place_s(σ(s))

rule: The top legend has one panel per color with a marker on its left or right side, meaning 'turn left' or 'turn right'. In the main area, the 8 block shoots block-wide rays in all four directions; a ray that hits a colored block turns left or right (relative to its heading) as the legend says for that color, and rays end at the grid edge. The output is the main area with the legend cropped off.
operator: turn: color → {L,R} from marker side in legend; for d ∈ {N,E,S,W}: ray from block with width w, on hitting block of color c set d := rot_{turn(c)}(d), continue until ∂Ω; Y = crop_main(X) + 8·⋃ rays

rule: Outside a 5-framed panel there is a legend of interlocking color pairs (a → b) plus a sample shape for each color a. Inside the panel, solid blocks of color a are replaced by a's sample shape recolored to b. The output is the framed panel cropped out.
operator: m: a→b from legend pairs, S_a = sample shape of a; Y = crop_frame(X) with each solid block B of color a replaced by m(a)·S_a placed at B

rule: A small 3x3 symmetric glyph on 7 gives a mask M. The 16x16 output tiles the complement of M with period 3, stretched so M's center becomes the 1-cell lattice nodes, its edge cells the 2-long line segments and its corner cells the 2x2 faces (cell is 0 where M=1, 7 where M=0). Then all 0s in the central 6x6 window turn into 9.

Four monochrome pieces are scattered; one holds a 2x2 color key. Assemble the four pieces, rotating as needed, into a solid rectangle (the key piece stays unrotated in the top-left), and color each piece with the key cell for the corner it occupies (TL, TR, BL, BR).
operator: pieces P_1..P_4, key K ∈ colors^{2×2}; find rotations ρ_i and placements t_i tiling a rectangle R exactly (P_key at TL, unrotated); Y = Σ_i K[corner(i)]·1[t_i + ρ_i(P_i)]

rule: The input splits into four equal quadrants. Output height = number of non-zero cells in the top-left quadrant, width = number in the top-right. The bottom-right quadrant is a stencil tiled over the output (by its minimal period), and its 0-cells take colors from the bottom-left quadrant indexed by tile position.
operator: H = |supp TL|, W = |supp TR|; T = BR reduced to its minimal period (p_h,p_w); Y[r,c] = T[r mod p_h, c mod p_w] if ≠0 else BL[(r div p_h) mod n, (c div p_w) mod n]

rule: Repair a drawing of colored rectilinear paths. Gaps are filled; 2-cells (corners/ends of unknown color) take their path's color. A 4 next to a path's corner redirects the path: the branch on the other side is erased and the path is extended through the 4 to the grid edge. At crossings one path is drawn over the other, usually the reverse of the input, but I could not find the rule that decides which.
operator: paths π_k (rectilinear, per color); Y = draw(π'_k) with π'_k = π_k with gaps closed, 2 → col(π_k), branch beyond a corner replaced by a ray through the adjacent 4 to ∂Ω; crossing cell color = col of the 'over' path (rule unknown)
missing: Over/under rule at crossings: flipping the input's crossing color works in 4 tasks' crossings but fails at train 3 (2,1); no color, orientation or marker rule found that fits every pair.

rule: The grid has two solid edge borders (two colors) and two noisy ones; an inner patterned rectangle has border lines of the same two colors on two of its sides. Output = the rectangle cropped (without its border lines) and transformed by the D4 element that sends each of its border colors to the grid edge of the same color.
operator: O = crop(object); find g ∈ D4 with g(side_O(c)) = side_grid(c) for both border colors c; Y = g(O)
